metadata.title: The role of openness to experience in innovating teaching and instruction through leader-member exchange and teacher creativity

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study collected cross-sectional survey data from teachers in Malaysia using a three-stage stratified random sampling procedure (states/regions, then schools within strata, then teachers within selected schools). The manuscript reports a response rate (35%) and provides descriptive characteristics (gender and urban/rural school location), but it does not report the use of complex survey weights or any specific sampling weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) in the estimation. The analytical approach is latent moderated structural equation modelling (LM-SEM) in Mplus with cluster-robust standard errors (TYPE = COMPLEX) to account for teachers nested within schools, rather than population-representative weighted estimation. Therefore, the results should be interpreted as model-based associations in the sampled teacher population, with clustering handled via robust SEs rather than survey-weighted inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable is an innovation indicator based on a single binary self-report item (whether a teacher implemented process innovations in the last 12 months), and the other constructs (LMX, openness, creativity) are Likert-scale latent variables. Plausible Values are not applicable because this is not an ILSA cognitive achievement assessment with PV-based scoring. The manuscript also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion or imputation), so the missing-data strategy is a reporting gap for transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were teachers working in schools in Malaysia. Sampling followed a three-stage stratified random procedure: (1) eight states across Malaysia’s regions were identified, (2) schools were selected within strata defined by urbanity (urban vs. rural) and school type (primary vs. secondary), and (3) teachers within selected schools were invited via principals’ distribution of a unique online questionnaire link. Inclusion required teachers to have at least one year of teaching experience. The survey was open for 15 weeks (Feb–May 2024) and reminders were sent bi-weekly; 3016 teachers completed the survey out of 8736 invited from 148 schools (35% response rate). The manuscript does not report additional item-level exclusions or missing-response rules beyond the SEM estimation approach.

The authors estimate latent moderated structural equation models in Mplus 8.5 using the WLSMV estimator for categorical/ordinal indicators and request cluster-robust standard errors (TYPE = COMPLEX) to address nesting of teachers within schools. Direct effects show openness to experience strongly predicts LMX (β = 0.397, p < .001) and teacher creativity (β = 0.956, p < .001), and teacher creativity predicts innovation (β = 0.271, p < .001), while LMX does not predict teacher creativity (β = −0.013, p = .219). Innovation is predicted by both teacher creativity (small effect) and LMX (β = 0.132, p < .001). Mediation is supported for openness via creativity and via LMX (total indirect effect β = 0.309, 95% CI [0.265, 0.351], p < .001), but moderated mediation is not supported (LMX interactions not significant). Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference) and lack of reported missing-data handling. data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is intentionally sparse because the manuscript does not train or evaluate any machine learning model (no predictive algorithms, no ML metrics such as accuracy/AUC/RMSE). Instead, it applies latent moderated structural equation modelling (SEM) with robust standard errors and bootstrapped mediation to test hypothesized relationships among latent constructs. As a result, fields required for empirical ML prediction (ml_techniques, main_findings with ML performance metrics, and PV handling) are not applicable in this schema.
